QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_26

question.text: A Cat III AIF's hurdle was raised from 10% to 12%. As per the workbook, Year 2 incentive fees:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook sensitivity in Example 2 shows that increasing the hurdle rate from 10% to 12% causes incentive fees to drop significantly, with Year 2 falling to Rs. 8,69,250 compared with the Rs. 41,99,250 produced under the 10% hurdle. A higher hurdle leaves less excess return over the hurdle, so incentive fees fall. The Trap: A higher hurdle reduces, not increases, incentive fees, and the methodology does not produce negative fees. Note: Per workbook pages 171-173.
